In philosophy there is a heuristic called Occam's Razor. It states, "Among competing hypotheses, the one with the fewest assumptions should be selected." It does not mean we should dismiss the competing hypotheses, but that we should examine the simplest one first. Sit down and try to work out all the logistics of the various claims and see how complicated it would get to determine all how all the components necessary for each idea to come out would be.

1) Terrorists hijack plane, terrorists fly plane into building, building collapses after a period of time due to the damage and subsequent fire caused by the plane.

Within this situation, we can reliably investigate the terrorists (background, purchases, activities, communications), their boarding and taking of the plane (location of their seats, armaments, the actual act of the hijacking), their operation of the plane (the flight path of the plane from ground control radar, the instrumentation of the plane from the black box, video and eyewitness testimony), and the resultant investigation collapse (structural modeling, forensic investigation, physical evidence). And those are just some of the overarching things to account for, as many other subordinate topics will have to be addressed.
